page: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is a compute-optimized instance powered by an AWS Graviton2 processor using the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture. It features 8 dedicated physical cores with 1 thread per core, running at a clock speed of 2.5 GHz. The processor includes 64 KB L1d cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 32 MB L3 cache. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing a resource density of 2.0 GB per core. It also includes a bundled 474 GB NVMe SSD local instance store volume and a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps, running on the Nitro hypervisor.

Benchmark data indicates balanced multi-core performance alongside some single-core limitations. The instance achieves average ratings in stress-ng single-core and multi-core tests, as well as average performance in software compilation and ray tracing via Geekbench. However, single-threaded tasks show weaker results, with a poor Geekbench single-core score of 930.0 and poor single-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth is robust for cached small blocks at 473.11 GB/sec, but drops to 116.89 GB/sec for uncached large blocks.

Given its ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation, the c6gd.2xlarge offers a cost-efficient profile for multi-threaded workloads that benefit from local NVMe storage. It demonstrates average performance in database operations and Redis SET operations, making it suitable for distributed databases, caching layers, and static web serving. It is less suited for heavy single-threaded processing or LLM inference, where text generation speeds remain weak to poor.
description: Amazon Web Services c6gd.2xlarge is an ARM64 compute-optimized instance powered by an 8-core AWS Graviton2 Neoverse-N1 processor running at 2.5 GHz. It features 16.0 GB of memory, a bundled 474 GB NVMe SSD local instance store, and 2 Gbps baseline network bandwidth on the Nitro hypervisor. Performance benchmarks show average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 12133.14 and Geekbench software compilation score of 8140.0. However, single-core performance is weaker, as evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0. The instance is highly cost-efficient for workloads requiring local high-speed storage and multi-threaded processing, such as database operations, Redis caching, and static web serving. It is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or large language model inference.
